"Option selling is a steady monthly income strategy."

It's one of the most dangerous half-truths in Indian markets.

Option selling wins often, in small amounts. That high win rate feels like income, right up until one event (a gap open, a policy surprise, a black-swan day) wipes out months of premium in a single session.

What separates serious option sellers:
• They always define their worst case, with hedges, spreads or strict stops.
• They respect margin. Being fully deployed on margin is not a strategy.
• They size for tail risk, not for the average week.
• They judge performance after the bad months, not during the good ones.

Selling options can be a great business when it's run like an insurance company: price the risk, diversify it and keep reserves. It goes badly when it's run like a lottery in reverse.

Option sellers: hedged or naked, and why? Let's discuss.
